```{r}
#| label: setup
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(plotly)

show_name <- "Game of Thrones"      # change this line to report on another show

episodes <- read.csv("data/episodes.csv")
one_show <- filter(episodes, show == show_name)

last_season <- max(one_show$season)
earlier     <- filter(one_show, season <  last_season)
final       <- filter(one_show, season == last_season)
lowest      <- head(arrange(one_show, rating), 1)
```

## `r show_name`: did the ending hold up?

`r show_name` has **`r nrow(one_show)` episodes** in our data.
Seasons 1 to `r last_season - 1` average
**`r round(mean(earlier$rating), 2)`** out of 10.
The final season averages **`r round(mean(final$rating), 2)`**.

One episode with the lowest rating (`r lowest$rating`) is "`r lowest$title`"
(season `r lowest$season`, episode `r lowest$episode`).

## Every episode

Move the mouse over a point to see the episode.

```{r}
#| label: fig-episodes
#| fig-cap: "Rating of every episode, in order of release."
p <- ggplot(one_show, aes(x = episode_no, y = rating)) +
  geom_line(colour = "grey70") +
  geom_point(aes(text = paste0("Season ", season, ", episode ", episode,
                               "<br>", title,
                               "<br>Rating: ", rating)),
             colour = "steelblue") +
  labs(x = "Episode (in order of release)", y = "Episode rating (out of 10)")

ggplotly(p, tooltip = "text")
```

## Average by season

```{r}
#| label: tbl-seasons
#| tbl-cap: "Number of episodes and average rating in each season."
season_avg <- one_show |>
  group_by(season) |>
  summarise(episodes = n(), average_rating = round(mean(rating), 2))

knitr::kable(season_avg)
```

## About this report

Data: TVmaze API, collected 11 November 2026. Ratings are TVmaze users' ratings
on that day, and they change. This report was built from `got_report.qmd`;
every number and chart above is calculated when the file is rendered.
